# Velocity

Velocity is a collection of tools that help reduce boilerplate/repetitive work for larger Xcode projects, especially in multi-developer environments.

It is part of an opinionated toolchain, and specific method of project management:

* The core Xcode project files are generated by [xcodegen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen).
* External dependencies are sourced using SwiftPM.
* Internal modules use the Velocity package system.
* Dependency injection uses the [Inject](https://github.com/jmfieldman/Inject) library (strongly recommended).

The benefits of using Velocity:

* External SwiftPM modules are cached/sourced on your local build environment: Xcode spends less time resolving dependencies.
* Xcodegen .yml files for all internal modules and external dependencies are generated automatically.
* Internal modules use api/implementation best practices, and integrate with Inject to automatically create top-level injection maps.
* Extremely minimal (almost negligible) module-creation overhead; lightweight modules encourage their proper use.

## Installation

Use Velocity as you would any other executable-based Swift package.

If you want a more streamlined execution experience, install Velocity 
using the [Mint Package Manager](https://github.com/yonaskolb/Mint).

```bash
# Install mint on your system, e.g.
$ brew install mint

# Install Velocity (recommended: bypass this using the Mintfile)
$ mint install jmfieldman/Velocity

# Run Velocity using Mint. This is the recommended method if you use a Mintfile
$ mint run velocity <..>
```

Once the Velocity commands are available, you typically put common invocations in a repeatable silo (e.g. a Makefile or shell scripts)

## Available Subcommands

This is a brief outline of available subcommands. 

### `pull-dependencies`

This command uses the `dependencies.yml` file to fetch your external SwiftPM-based dependencies and store them in local silo, separate from the standard SwiftPM toolchain. This allows Xcode to view them as local path-based packages, and skip unwanted remote version resolution.

### `generate-imports`

Searches through the source files of your Velocity packages. It generates an `imports.yml` file for each module, that lists each dependency. This `imports.yml` file is used by other tools to build up xcodegen yml files.

### `generate-xcodegen`

Generates a `project-modules.yml` xcodegen file. This yml contains all of the target declarations for every module in your project, and can be included in your main project xcodegen yml file.

### `generate-xcodegen-deps`

Generates a `project-dependencies.yml` xcodegen file. This yml contains all of the xcodegen target declarations for every external module listen in the `dependencies.yml` file, and can be included in your main project xcodegen yml file.

### `generate-inject`

Identifies the injectable api/implementation classes, and generates an Inject-compatible top-level injection function. This function is executed immediately at app launch to register your injection map.

### `sanitize-xcodegen-project`

The nature of Xcodegen is to rebuild your Project.xcodeproj file on each invocation. This updates the timestamps of your project and can lead to unnecessary work during incremental builds. This command examines module and project changes, cleans out dirty modules from DerivedData, and resets project file timestamps to a previous date if no project changes were made. This can help speed up incremental builds.
